extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy, literary critics, humor theorists, and writers/stage practitioners studying the theory of the comic
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts Bergson's analytic criteria for what makes something comic across forms (physiognomy, gesture, situation, words, character) and his account of the social function of laughter. Useful for analysing or producing comic effects informed by Bergson's essay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Le comique n'existe qu'à l'intérieur de ce qui est proprement humain
rubrics_metrics.description: «Il n'y à pas de comique en dehors de ce qui est proprement humain.» Objects or animals provoke laughter only insofar as they bear a human resemblance (attitude, form, use) — the comic is tied to human behavior, conventions and uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: one laughs at an animal only when it displays a human attitude; one laughs at a hat only because of the human shape/usage impressed on it. Implication for creators: ensure comic elements map to recognizably human traits; anti-pattern: purely natural landscapes or non-human phenomena are not intrinsically comic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Le rire exige l'indifférence (anesthésie du cœur)
rubrics_metrics.description: The comic only works when it 'falls on a calm, even surface of soul' — emotion (pity, strong feeling) is the principal enemy of laughter. Laughter addresses 'intelligence pure' and requires a temporary muting of sympathetic feeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical note: to produce laughter, frame the scene so the audience can take a detached, spectator stance (e.g., ironic distance, neutral presentation). Anti-pattern: scenes that stir strong pity or pathos will block comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Le rire est social et requiert un écho (force d'expansion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Laughter is essentially a group phenomenon — it wants to reverberate, to be echoed; we often only laugh when we are part of the laughing group. Many comic effects depend upon shared social codes and audience contagion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: jokes that succeed in a full theatre may fail for an isolated listener; some effects are culture-specific. For performers/writers: consider audience context and collective resonance; anti-pattern: standalone/completely private comic gestures that lack social echo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Le comique naît de l'automatisme, de la raideur, du mécanisme
rubrics_metrics.description: A central law: comic effects arise to the extent that a human being appears mechanical or governed by automatism — rigidity of movement, thought or character produces the risible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations: a runner who keeps moving into a fall, a person who mechanically dips pen into a fake inkwell. For creators: emphasize mechanical repetition, rigidity or failure to adapt; anti-pattern: displaying supple, responsive behavior that signals 'grace'.

rubrics_metrics.name: L'effet est d'autant plus comique que la cause parait naturelle et connaissable
rubrics_metrics.description: When the audience can perceive and reconstruct the natural origin of the comic cause, the effect becomes funnier: the more natural/traceable the cause, the stronger the comic reaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a distraction appears funnier if we see it originate and grow. Practical tip: reveal the genesis of the mishap or quirk incrementally to increase comic payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comique des formes (physionomie comique = expression fixée / grimace)
rubrics_metrics.description: A comic physiognomy is one that suggests a permanent, fixed grimace or contracted fold — an expression that looks crystallized and unchanging, as if the person's inner life had been petrified into a mechanical attitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a tic consolidated into a fixed expression, a face that always seems to be laughing/crying/whistling. Caricature exploits and amplifies these latent fixities. For artists: render static, habitual facial dispositions; anti-pattern: expressive faces that read as mobile, nuanced, or 'graceful'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Le caricaturiste révèle la grimace latente par l'exagération instrumentale
rubrics_metrics.description: Caricature makes visible a motion already suggested in nature by exaggerating it; exaggeration must feel like a means to reveal a pre-existing tendency, not as an end in itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline for caricature: distort along the direction already implied by the natural form (e.g., lengthen a nose in the way it already tends to 'want' to lengthen). Anti-pattern: gratuitous exaggeration that does not correspond to an underlying, readable tendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comique des mouvements (gestes risibles = suggestion d'une mécanique interne)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gestures, attitudes and movements are comic to the extent that the human body suggests a simple, mechanical apparatus — especially when movements are repetitive, stereotyped or fail to vary with changing situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: an orator whose gesture repeats mechanically; an action that imitates a tool's motion (sawing, ringing an imaginary bell). For staging: emphasize repetition and predictable timing; anti-pattern: gestures that organically follow evolving inner states.

rubrics_metrics.name: L'imitation met en lumière le caractère mécanique et rend risible
rubrics_metrics.description: A previously unnoticed gesture becomes laughable when imitated: imitation extracts and isolates the mechanical, uniform aspect that can be reproduced, thereby revealing its comic nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance tip: mimicry can expose automatism and make it comic. Anti-pattern: imitation that targets genuinely spontaneous, varied behavior (which resists imitation) will not be comic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comique de caractère (vice comme cadre rigide, types «communs»)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain vices or fixed dispositions act like an external framework imposed on the person; such rigid traits (obsessions, an idée fixe) produce comic characters — often typified with common nouns (e.g., 'le Jaloux', 'l'Avare').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Don Quixote as systematic distraction; Ménalque-type distractees. For writers: create characters whose defining flaw is externalized and repeatable. Anti-pattern: psychologically integrated vices that are absorbed into complex, tragic persons (which tend toward drama, not comedy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Le comique est inconscience: le personnage comique s'ignore lui‑même
rubrics_metrics.description: A comic character is generally comical in the exact measure that they are unaware of their own ridiculousness; awareness transforms or diminishes the comic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: defects that seek to hide themselves when perceived; Harpagon would show his avarice differently if aware. For performers: portray obliviousness rather than self-conscious performance. Anti-pattern: characters who perform their defect with deliberate irony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Le rire a une fonction sociale corrective (châtiment par l'humiliation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Laughter functions as a social gesture: it punishes or intimidates eccentricities and raideurs that threaten sociability — not always justly, and often without reflection on individual circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implications: comic devices can serve to enforce social norms or to make members self-correct. Ethical note: laughter's punitive edge may be malicious or unfair; creators should be aware of the social consequences of ridicule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Le comique s'oppose à la grâce (raideur plutôt que laideur)
rubrics_metrics.description: The comic is better characterized as 'raideur' (stiffness) opposed to 'grace' (elasticity), rather than as simple ugliness; it's the loss of supple adaptation that makes things risible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design/composition tip: highlight lack of elasticity in body, mind or character to produce comic contrast with expected grace. Anti-pattern: focusing on mere ugliness without suggesting mechanical inflexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Le comique peut naître d'une situation accidentelle ou devenir interne au caractère
rubrics_metrics.description: Initially comic effects are often accidental, caused by external circumstances; but they may become internalized when the raideur or automatism is part of the person's nature and supplies its own repeated occasions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example progression: from a stumbling passerby (accident) to a habitual distracted person (internalized comic). For narrative: consider whether the comic is situational (one-off) or character-based (recurring, cumulative).

rubrics_metrics.name: L'effet comique peut croître par répétition et crescendo (effet onirique/du rêve)
rubrics_metrics.description: Repetition, accumulation and a gradual march toward absurdity can produce a dreamlike comedic crescendo (e.g., refrains, scenes that escalate from reasonable to extravagant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use repetition and increasing eccentricity to produce a hypnotic, dreamlike comic effect (examples: Molière's plays, song refrains). Beware of overrepetition that loses intelligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comique de mots et de situations: déformation du sens, incompréhension, jeux de mots
rubrics_metrics.description: Words and situations become comic when meaning is emptied, deformed or displaced (e.g., speech in half-sleep, misunderstandings, the 'souffleur' scene). Such comic effects often rely on semantic breakdown or equivocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writerly tip: exploit ambiguity, mishearing, slip-of-the-tongue and literal/figurative confusions to create verbal comedy. Anti-pattern: relying on purely abstract 'intellectual contrasts' without social or embodied anchoring — Bergson warns that such abstract contrasts don't explain why we laugh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Le rire part du tac au tac et n'est pas toujours réfléchi ou juste
rubrics_metrics.description: Laughter is a quick, habitual reaction (a tacit riposte) rather than a considered judgment; as such it may err, strike innocents, and function by long social habit more than by individual equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical caution: creators and analysts should recognize that comic laughter can be crude and unjust; designers of satire should consider this limit when targeting individuals vs. types.
